transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A burning smell usually indicates either a large amount of fluff/lint has built up on the heater element (which can smoulder) or an electrical component is overheating. Please switch off and unplug the dryer immediately. Once it is cool, please check two things:
1. Is the main fluff filter in the door opening heavily clogged with lint?
2. Is the vent hose at the back of the machine kinked or blocked? If you find a large amount of lint or a blockage, clean it thoroughly. If the smell persists after cleaning, or if you see any scorch marks or smoke, do not use the dryer again and call an engineer.

ok I've switched it off at the wall already?? the filter is really full, it hasn't been cleaned for a few weeks. the hose is squashed behind the dryer and there's fluff inside the end. is that what caused it??

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, that combination of a very full filter and a squashed hose with fluff inside is probably what caused it. The lint builds up on the heater element where it gets extremely hot; if airflow is restricted by the blocked vent, that lint can smoulder and create a burning smell. This is a fire risk, so please do not use the dryer until you have cleared these blockages completely. To be safe, please unplug the machine again and perform two checks:
1. Remove the condenser unit (usually behind a flap at the bottom front) and rinse it under the tap to remove any fluff buildup.
2. Check inside the drum for any small items like socks or coins that may have fallen into the gap between the drum and the outer tub, as these can also overheat. Once you have done this, let me know if you found anything else blocked.
mine is a vented one with a hose out the wall, so I don't think it has a condenser?? I haven't looked in the drum for anything. is it safe to use again once the filter and hose are cleaned??

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The burning smell usually means that lint has built up on the heater element or in the ducting, which can smoulder and create a fire risk. Please unplug the machine and clear the vent hose completely; if there is fluff inside the end of the hose, it needs to be removed with a vacuum or a flexible brush. Once you have done that, let me know what you find.
I haven't cleaned it yet, it's wedged in a cupboard and I'm nervous about pulling it out?? Can I run it again once the filter and hose are cleaned, or does it need an engineer to look at it first??

⚠ Stop using this appliance
I understand being nervous about moving a heavy appliance wedged in a cupboard. The burning smell is almost probably caused by the lint buildup and restricted airflow we discussed; however, because there was smoke/smell, it must not be used again until the blockage is fully cleared and the machine has been inspected for damage. Please do not attempt to run it yet. If you cannot safely pull the dryer out yourself, please call a qualified engineer to clear the vent hose and check the internal wiring and heater element for scorch marks or damage before putting it back into service.
